style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>We see in the data that </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/aa05bbe1-28db-460e-9d87-19deb298da44?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;"><span>AI engineering is seeing explosive demand</span></a><span>, and that forward deployed engineers (FDEs) are also seeing </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/a31ab315-602f-4087-8fa5-2fd8c686a440?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;"><span>a massive spike in demand</span></a><span>. </span><em><span>For more detail on this, check our deepdive on </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/f7d6755c-a053-41db-8fe8-b647bdc70545?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;"><span>what FDEs are, and why they’re hot right now.</span></a></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Anecdotal evidence from job seekers suggests that being in these fields means the market is as good as it gets, right now:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>“It’s the greatest job market I’ve ever seen. </span></strong><span>I’m an L5 former FDE, now SWE, who has worked on LLM apps for ~2 years. The inbound top of the funnel is bonkers, and I find myself saying “no” to places that I would have once killed to work at.”</span><em><span> – AI Engineer at an AI decacorn, San Francisco, US</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“I have seen huge interest in FDEs and AI Engineers as an engineer who’s been interviewing.”</span><em><span> – Software Engineer, 5 YOE, New York, US</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“It’s not hard to get interviews as an ML/AI engineer. The technical bar is about the same as late 2022. If anything, onsites seem to be of fewer rounds for the same level. Companies seem to move fast to get candidates onsite.”</span><em><span> – ML engineer, ex-Meta, Bay Area, US</span></em></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>An engineer at Apple is surprised by the demand for their skills from AI companies:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“Got a lot of responses from cold applications for AI roles, and ended up with two offers at AI infra companies. I ended up getting a significant pay bump beyond what Apple offers for the same level!”</span></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>A software engineer at well-known company in the Bay Area, also finds the job market is good:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“I got offers for Senior SWE with Stripe and Rippling, was rejected from Snowflake… Anecdotally, the job market is better compared to 2025 for regular SWE positions in the Valley.”</span></p></blockquote><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);"><span>EM and Staff+ profiles are near-impossible to fill</span></h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>A repeat complaint from hiring managers in the US is how challenging it is to recruit solid engineering managers and Staff+ engineers:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>“It’s extremely difficult to hire EMs and Staff+ engineers.</span></strong><span> It’s much easier to hire folks with less than 10 years of experience. This is despite us offering 90th percentile comp via Pave, and having a hybrid and good culture.”</span><em><span> – Fractional VP of Engineering, Series B, New York, US</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“My team has been looking for a new engineering manager for three months and we barely had any good applicants. It’s a super weird dynamic right now.” </span><em><span>– Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Series D Fintech, company with offices in the US and EU</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>“The most desirable candidates right now are EM or staff-level folks who can keep up with uncertainty in the business.</span></strong><span> We are having trouble hiring folks who roll with the constant change that is now very typical at startups.”</span><em><span> – CTO at a San Francisco-based startup</span></em></p></blockquote><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);"><span>“Specialist” profiles are hard to recruit</span></h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>A few examples:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>Distributed systems engineers: “</span></strong><span>We can’t find enough qualified distributed systems engineers, cloud infra etc. I have 20 reqs [open positions] right now.”</span><em><span> – Recruiter at a hyperscaler, US</span></em></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>Product engineers: </span></strong><span>“‘Product engineer’ has been a hard profile to find. It is also hard to find someone with a decent design eye who can also build full stack. The hardest thing to hire for has been taste + trust… I’d rather hire someone who is ‘behind’ on AI, but has great taste/judgment than someone with complex agent setups and prompt libraries.”</span><em><span> – Tech Lead, seed-stage startup, Los Angeles, US</span></em></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>Senior engineers, in general: </span></strong><span>“As a hiring manager trying to hire seniors right now, it has felt pretty difficult. Most applicants are totally unqualified, and the qualified ones do poorly in an interview.”</span><em><span> – Engineering manager, robotics company, Canada</span></em></p></li></ul><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);"><span>Silence for many</span></h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>One in five respondents detail how difficult it has been to get responses from recruiters:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“Things are looking bleak. Now, applications are going into a void. Recruiters aren’t reaching out immediately as before. Of 10 or so applications sent out, I’ve gotten one interview scheduled that was then rescinded because it looks like the team was laid off.”</span><em><span> – Frontend engineer, 10+ YOE, Southeast US</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“The job market has been a desert. I’ve gotten back into applying, job agencies seem to have few roles they’re looking to fill. The companies I have applied to myself, never reply.”</span><em><span> – Software Engineer, 8 YOE, Southern California</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“Recruiters are ghosting me! Every time when I respond to recruiter reachouts, they ALL ghosted me after a few messages and have similar stories from friends.”</span><em><span> – Software Engineer, 7 YOE, ex-Meta, Switzerland</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“So far, I have a hard time even getting past the hiring manager and I’m rejected before I can do the proper technical assessment.”</span><em><span> – Software Engineer, 7 YOE, Helsinki, Finland</span></em></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Even folks at Big Tech face a lack of response. Here’s a Technical Program Manager currently at Meta who used to be very in-demand:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“I put a few feelers out when Meta announced layoffs, and it’s just radio silence. I don’t want to sound cocky, but with my resume, you at least get a chat with a recruiter, usually right away. But Google and Anthropic just ghosted me.”</span></p></blockquote><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span>4. Higher hiring bar & lower compensation – but not for everyone</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>In a “normal” market, when the hiring bar goes up, so does compensation. 16px;line-height: 26px;display: none;"></div><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);"><span>Very picky hiring managers</span></h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>A few examples:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“</span><strong><span>Out of my last 100 or so candidates that got to the on-site interviews, we extended two offers. </span></strong><span>It’s just hard to get quality applicants for senior-level positions.”</span><em><span> – Engineering Manager, mid-sized company, hiring remote across the US</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“I just talked to one of my colleagues who interviewed 150+ folks for a mid-level position, and is about to give up because none clear the bar.”</span><em><span> – Director of Engineering, Big Tech, US</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>“From 2,000 applications for software engineers and data engineers, 10-20 make it to culture fit interviews</span></strong><span>, about 3-6 make it to culture fit, and 1-2 get an offer. Our interview round has resume screening, recruiter call, and a take-home exercise, before the culture fit interview.”</span><em><span> – Recruiter, deep tech company, Helsinki, Finland</span></em></p></blockquote><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);"><span>Some AI-native companies struggling to hire in the Bay Area</span></h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>AI-native startups have raised large funding rounds, pay at the very top of the market – and yet some founders find it hard to recruit. Here’s a CTO at such a startup in San Francisco:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“There are three groups of people we see on the market:</span></p><ol style="margin-left: 20px;margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>People who don’t “get” AI.</span></strong><span> Enough said.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>“Slop cannons:”</span></strong><span> they use AI, but don’t grok fundamentals, don’t pay any attention to code quality, and think it’s okay to yolo stuff to prod because they’ve never worked on real systems</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>Truly exceptional people: </span></strong><span><span>they “get” AI and have autonomy. They are either joining the AI labs, or getting Y Combinator funding and starting their own company.</span><br><br><span>It’s hard to hire!”</span></span></p></li></ol></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>The problem seems to be that anyone who is </span><em><span>good enough</span></em><span> for this startup to recruit, also has the option to start their own company, and in San Francisco, they often do. </span><em><span>This could explain why more SF-based startups also hire remotely, even in their early stages.</span></em></p><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);"><span>Higher interview bar</span></h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>A fullstack engineer with three years of experience in the US explains:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“It’s easy to get interviews, but the bar to pass them is higher than in 2022. For leetcode [data structure and algorithms interview], you not only have to get the optimal solution, but have to be quick too, and not fumble. Since many people can solve them because of resources like Neetcode, the bottleneck is speed.”</span></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>Interviews are changing, and AI-related exercises are becoming normal. </span></strong><span>A lead fullstack engineer in Germany told us:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“Interviews have changed, a LOT! In the past, questions would include things like React vs Angular, Java vs Go. Today it’s ‘can you one-shot a waterfall spec to derive a product in two hours that would otherwise take 10 years?’ Either you go with it and get a job offer, or you push back and explain the problems with it, and then you don’t.”</span></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>A hiring manager based in Prague, Czechia, says candidates don’t do well when tested on AI skills:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“We recently introduced a hiring baseline requiring AI skills, and we find a lot of the candidates have no concrete experience using AI tools.”</span></p></blockquote><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);"><span>Compensation seems lower</span></h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>A few data points:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span>A software engineer in Southern California: “A Walmart contractor role for a remote ‘Web Engineer’ offered $140K and zero benefits (no PTO [paid time off], bonuses; no insurance).”</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span>A principal engineer in the Southwest US: “As a principal engineer, I received a few offers for Senior-level positions that were less than I made as a Senior, pre-2020!”</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span>A software engineer in the UK: “Pay bands are all over the place. I’ve seen some at £80k (terrible!) and others ranging from £125k–£200k (great!).”</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>One reality at present is that it’s an employer’s market, meaning they get to choose what to pay. </span></strong><span>As a founder at a seed-stage startup in the Bay Area tells us:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“It’s an employer’s market. I’m getting interest from principal engineers from Snowflake for a $250K base salary position because they got laid off.”</span></p></blockquote><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);"><span>Mid-year hiring seems to be down</span></h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>A software engineer in the US reckons there’s something about the middle of the year being quiet:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“I interviewed around a little in January 2026. I always got responses from recruiters, usually within a day. Now, in June 2026, it’s night and day: my own company just cut 50% of staff at our board’s demand.”</span></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Data on the job market confirms that hiring is seasonal, and mostly happens during the first six months of the year:</span></p><div July-December. Source: </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/655fa96e-2b26-4f4b-bfd0-e8510d87055c?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="text-decoration: underline;"><span>Part 1</span></a></em></figcaption></figure></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Sadly, offers were rescinded for a few correspondents:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“I finished the process with PayPal and we were in the hiring committee phase, but they cut 20% of their workforce because of AI.”</span><em><span> – Software Engineer, 8 YOE, US</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“A dev I know left for a new role and got a call the week beforehand, letting them know their position was cancelled as part of layoffs. Another friend joined a mutual’s YC company and got laid off within three months.”</span><em><span> – founder, Bay Area, US</span></em></p></blockquote><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span>5. Engineering leader & IC recruitment are equally weird</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Hiring managers complain how hard it is to recruit hands-on engineering leaders, at the same time as hands-on engineering leaders find it harder than ever to get hired! It’s the same paradox as mentioned above, suggesting that on some level it’s harder for people and employers to connect these days.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>A CTO in San Francisco is encountering a very weird market:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“I left my CTO job at the beginning of the year. I joined another early-stage startup as a CTO, but got burnt… Anecdotally, it feels like the market is fairly ‘hot’ in head-of-eng and CTO jobs, BUT here’s the weird thing: </span><strong><span>there are now lots of engineering leaders who are either part-time contracting, or building in stealth, like me.</span></strong><span> This is because taking one of these jobs would mean taking a pay cut, or finding yourself in a higher stress/more invasive work-life balance position, post-job change.”</span></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>That engineering leadership roles are being interpreted very differently doesn’t help things, either. From a head of engineering in the UK:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>“I’ve seen a huge difference in specs/responsibilities for eng manager and head of eng roles. </span></strong><span>Some very hands-on with people management, and others essentially slimmed down to be an IC who happens to manage. Pay bands are all over the place… The market isn’t as good as I remember a few years ago, but it does seem buoyant, particularly for people willing to cross over a bit more and not just do pure people management or pure IC work.”</span></p></blockquote><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span>6. US market trends</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Here are some current trends in the US:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>Folks experiencing the “best market ever” are in the US. </span></strong><span>These are AI engineering, ML engineers, forward-deployed engineers, and a few Big Tech folks with very strong networks. The same roles are not enjoying truly standout conditions in places like the UK and the EU – or perhaps there are just fewer of them.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>Product engineering demand is much stronger in the US. </span></strong><span>An AI Engineer in Europe observed that most applied AI roles are in the US, while in places like the UK, most companies hire forward-deployed engineers.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>The “talent shortage” complaint is more common in the US. </span></strong><span>Startups struggling to hire senior+ engineers, and Big Tech looking for infrastructure engineers, are US-headquartered. In contrast, hiring managers at EU companies describe being overwhelmed with inbound applications, and needing to put in a lot of work to find quality applicants.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>Tech layoffs seem to be flooding tech hubs in the US. </span></strong><span>Reports of hiring managers getting applications from standout engineers who were let go from places like Amazon, Microsoft, Snowflake, and similar companies are all in the US. That might be because it’s harder to execute mass layoffs in Europe, meaning that fewer occurred. Big Tech has a smaller presence in Europe, which could be a factor.</span></p></li></ul><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span>7. Trends in the UK, EU, & rest of the world</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Here are factors specific to the UK, EU, and Canada:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>“Ghosting” is far more common than in the US. </span></strong><span>Not hearing back from recruiters, or recruiters not responding after replying to a reachout, comes up a lot among folks in the EU. In contrast, in the US, solid software engineers seem to be getting interviews easier, it’s just harder to get an offer.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>“Fake applicants” seem a bigger problem in Europe. </span></strong><span>The issue of “fakers” with potential links to hostile governments is mentioned mostly by EU and UK companies. It might be that such folks get caught more often in Europe, where an interviewer might be more likely to use the local language and expose a fake candidate’s own lack of language ability.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>Remote roles are rare, almost everything is hybrid. </span></strong><span>The disappearance of full-remote roles is a repeated complaint in the EU.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span>Language is a blocker. </span></strong><span>Job seekers in Germany and Czechia report being rejected from software engineering jobs for not speaking the local language at a native level. In Czechia, a hiring manager told us of their frustration caused by having a hard requirement of only proceeding with applicants with native or high-level proficiency in the local language.</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>Not being able to move jobs due to a “compensation ceiling” is a problem repeatedly mentioned in the EU and Brazil. </span></strong><span>Two cases:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“I’m struggling to find a job that pays more than what I currently make – it’s weird. I am at the Staff level at a consultancy. So far, in eight months, I got rejected instantly, save for one screening call.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>I have a friend in a similar position, also “stuck” because they cannot get a higher offer than what they make now. He is working in Amazon and so far he has gotten five interviews, likely because he has Amazon in his resume. But all offers come in well below what he makes.”</span><em><span> – Software Engineer, Krakow, Poland</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“Compensation is the problem, and the reason I don’t bother responding to inbound opportunities. I wasn’t receiving any messages in my LinkedIn inbox until two or three weeks ago. However, all the ones with compensation listed are paying less than what I’m earning, and the ones without comp listed are lower tier companies that will probably pay low as well. Have been dismissing all the recruiters so far.”</span><em><span> – Senior fullstack engineer, 8 YOE, Brazil</span></em></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>In all fairness, the reason some people are hitting this compensation ceiling is because there </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/6c759554-556d-4a26-83e2-65277581e99b?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;"><span>are fewer “top-tier” (Tier 3) positions</span></a><span> in Europe than in the US. </span><em><span>We cover more on the </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/6c759554-556d-4a26-83e2-65277581e99b?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;"><span>Trimodal nature of software engineering compensation.</span></a></em></p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span>Takeaways</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>It was very useful to talk with people about what the hiring market is like as a job seeker or a hiring manager. Of course, data is very useful but data on the market we covered in </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/655fa96e-2b26-4f4b-bfd0-e8510d87055c?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;"><span>Part 1</span></a><span> and </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/a14312a4-0299-45c7-bc0a-0d416c4c3313?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;"><span>Part 2</span></a><span> of this series doesn’t quite capture how strange today’s market is:</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>A small group is seeing the best-ever recruitment market: </span></strong><span>AI Engineers, ML Engineers, FDEs and a few folks with exceptional experience and connections. These engineers are more in demand than ever, getting higher compensation than ever at AI companies. For example, here’s the </span><em><span>median</span></em><span> total compensation offered by various larger tech companies:</span></p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: Engineers that AI labs and other “hot” companies want to hire: these are the folks that pretty much all other AI companies are also looking for.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>Most companies are finding it hard to hire senior folks, but their expectations have gone up! </span></strong><span>Finding senior engineers and engineering leaders is equally hard. What is unsaid by hiring managers is that their expectations have gone up, but how much they are willing to pay has often not! Also, the massive increase in AI-enhanced resumes does not help, and is making inbound referrals useless.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>Solid software engineers are not getting responses or offers, unless via referrals. </span></strong><span>The majority of people I spoke with, who are on the job market, see it as very bad, and get few to no responses for applications they put out there; even when they do, offers can be withdrawn at the last minute.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>This happens while the data shows that the number of open software engineering jobs keeps </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/655fa96e-2b26-4f4b-bfd0-e8510d87055c?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;"><span>going up.</span></a><span> So, why are they not seeing more opportunities?</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>My sense is that the job market is somewhat worse in the UK and EU. </span></strong><span>Job seekers complain more about ghosting and being lowballed in compensation. I wonder if some of this has to do with how all leading AI labs are headquartered in the US, and more US startups have successfully pivoted to become “AI-native.” Plus, the majority of AI funding comes from US VCs, and often to companies headquartered in the Bay Area.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>As AI is the single biggest growth area in the tech industry, anyone and everyone close to this space will see more and better opportunities; be that in funding, jobs, or career advancement.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>How are things for you as a hiring manager or job seeker? Please leave a comment about what you see on the market.</span></p><p class="button-wrapper"
